relations.myth: God commissions Uriel to warn Noah
relations.note: God hears the angels’ appeal and sends Uriel to warn Noah.

relations.myth: Four angels petition God over earthly bloodshed
relations.note: Uriel and Michael jointly observe human violence and appeal to God.

relations.myth: Four angels petition God over earthly bloodshed
relations.note: Uriel and Raphael jointly observe human violence and appeal to God.

relations.myth: Four angels petition God over earthly bloodshed
relations.note: Uriel and Gabriel jointly observe human violence and appeal to God.

relations.myth: Burial of Adam and Abel in Paradise
relations.note: God orders Michael and Uriel to wrap and bury Adam and Abel.

relations.myth: Uriel wrestles the incarnate archangel Israel
relations.note: Uriel wrestles Jacob, whose heavenly identity is the superior archangel Israel.

relations.myth: Dispute over heavenly precedence
relations.note: Uriel contests angelic rank with Israel, who claims precedence over him.

relations.myth: Angelic interpretation of Ezra’s apocalypse
relations.note: Jeremiel answers waiting souls within the same apocalypse interpreted chiefly by Uriel.
Some commentators propose Jeremiel as a textual substitution or alternate identity for Uriel.

relations.myth: Angels bring souls from darkness to judgment
relations.note: Uriel and Barakiel jointly bring human souls before God’s judgment.

relations.myth: Angels bring souls from darkness to judgment
relations.note: Uriel and Ramiel jointly bring human souls before God’s judgment.

relations.myth: Angels bring souls from darkness to judgment
relations.note: Uriel and Samiel jointly bring human souls before God’s judgment.

relations.myth: Angels bring souls from darkness to judgment
relations.note: Uriel and Azael jointly bring human souls before God’s judgment.

relations.myth: Administration of Adam’s material body
relations.note: Uriel belongs to the subordinate bodily administration within Yaldabaoth’s created order.

relations.myth: Seven rulers govern demons of bodily members
relations.note: Michael and Uriel are named together among seven rulers over bodily demons.

relations.myth: Seven rulers govern demons of bodily members
relations.note: Asmenedas and Uriel are named together among seven rulers over bodily demons.

relations.myth: Seven rulers govern demons of bodily members
relations.note: Saphasatoel and Uriel are named together among seven rulers over bodily demons.

relations.myth: Seven rulers govern demons of bodily members
relations.note: Aarmouriam and Uriel are named together among seven rulers over bodily demons.

relations.myth: Seven rulers govern demons of bodily members
relations.note: Richram and Uriel are named together among seven rulers over bodily demons.

relations.myth: Seven rulers govern demons of bodily members
relations.note: Amiorps and Uriel are named together among seven rulers over bodily demons.
Early Enoch witnesses alternate Sariel and Uriel at key textual loci.
Later angelologies harmonize Uriel with Phanuel, though Enochic evidence distinguishes them.
The Zohar explicitly treats the western light Nuriel as Uriel.
Comparative angelology equates them through eschatological functions, without early Islamic support.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Uriel and Raphael appear jointly in Eastern Orthodox synaxes and icons.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Uriel and Gabriel appear jointly in Eastern Orthodox synaxes and icons.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Uriel and Michael appear jointly in Eastern Orthodox synaxes and icons.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Uriel and Selaphiel appear jointly in Eastern Orthodox synaxes and icons.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Uriel and Jehudiel appear jointly in Eastern Orthodox synaxes and icons.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Uriel and Barachiel appear jointly in Eastern Orthodox synaxes and icons.

relations.myth: Collective commemoration of the chief archangels
relations.note: Some Eastern Orthodox lists commemorate Jeremiel jointly with Uriel.

relations.myth: Uriel receives Christ’s blood and water
relations.note: Uriel receives blood and water from Christ’s wounded side for Ethiopia.

relations.myth: Christ’s blood sanctifies Ethiopian sacred sites
relations.note: Later Ethiopian versions make Michael accompany Uriel in dispersing Christ’s blood.

relations.myth: Satan tricks Uriel into revealing Paradise
relations.note: Disguised as a cherub, Satan deceives Uriel into pointing out Paradise.

relations.myth: Uriel warns Gabriel of Eden’s intruder
relations.note: Uriel recognizes Satan’s deception and warns Gabriel that an evil spirit entered Eden.
